Configuration allocates no graph nodes; compose creates a complete runtime.
Defaults are immutable, diagnostics defaults to off, and local overrides only
select name/diagnostics. Distinct instances use distinct names, input Nodes and
resource bindings. A name is not an authorization token.
Display components receive only the original `.view`; frameworks pass the original
identity/execution/retained capabilities; maintainers inspect the same Graph.
Showing an identity subset does not remove lifecycle or retained-evidence nodes.
Capabilities have no arbitrary I/O execution method. The application keeps the
original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's
original references without introducing another identity registry.
| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |
| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |
| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |
| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |
| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |
| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |
| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |
For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records
per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. A busy or exhausted
write budget produces an exact cancelled/no-submit result; there is no queue or
automatic retry. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or
proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application
must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery.
The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended.
The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination
are distinct. Retention remains bounded by the existing contract, not by whether
someone is viewing the graph. The demo's final forced test cleanup does not prove
The private value binding clears stale values on INVALIDATE and ERROR. The existing
public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter currently ignores INVALIDATE, so it is not a
direct substitute for this particular view contract.
Follow the actual request, admission and outcome references in the demo output to
the running graph. Then distinguish these three questions:
| Did this node's implementation change despite unchanged ID/edges? | Revision-bound source mapping within its declared coverage |
| Who changed it? | Separate provenance; an implementation digest alone gives no attribution |
| Which consequences remain unchanged? | Independent verification bound to the current revision and inputs |
Missing source binding means uncovered; missing provenance means unknown. An old
receipt does not verify a new implementation. Existing bounded source-change and
mutation evidence can be inspected in the [implementation review](../../docs/design/causal-graded-entry-implementation/README.md).
Those retained artifacts describe their own revisions; the new demo does not
requalify them or attest the loaded production source.

Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | `graph.describe()` for graph structure; the instance's `inspect()` for host state, documented in [host](causal-focused-host.ts) | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. The application keeps the"},{"line":92,"text":"original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. An old"},{"line":136,"text":"receipt does not verify a new implementation. Existing bounded source-change and"},{"line":137,"text":"mutation evidence can be inspected in the [implementation review](../../docs/design/causal-graded-entry-implementation/README.md)."},{"line":138,"text":"Those retained artifacts describe their own revisions; the new demo does not"},{"line":139,"text":"requalify them or attest the loaded production source."},{"line":140,"text":""},{"line":141,"text":"The example and offline tests demonstrate available composition paths, not a"},{"line":142,"text":"human usability result or superiority to a complete plain-code host. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application keeps the"},{"line":92,"text":"original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. A busy or exhausted"},{"line":109,"text":"write budget produces an exact cancelled/no-submit result; there is no queue or"},{"line":110,"text":"automatic retry. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Retention remains bounded by the existing contract, not by whether"},{"line":117,"text":"someone is viewing the graph. An old"},{"line":136,"text":"receipt does not verify a new implementation. Existing bounded source-change and"},{"line":137,"text":"mutation evidence can be inspected in the [implementation review](../../docs/design/causal-graded-entry-implementation/README.md)."},{"line":138,"text":"Those retained artifacts describe their own revisions; the new demo does not"},{"line":139,"text":"requalify them or attest the loaded production source."},{"line":140,"text":""},{"line":141,"text":"The example and offline tests demonstrate available composition paths, not a"},{"line":142,"text":"human usability result or superiority to a complete plain-code host. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | `graph.describe()` for graph structure; the instance's `inspect()` for host state, documented in [host](causal-focused-host.ts) | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. The application keeps the"},{"line":92,"text":"original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. An old"},{"line":136,"text":"receipt does not verify a new implementation. The application keeps the"},{"line":92,"text":"original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. A busy or exhausted"},{"line":109,"text":"write budget produces an exact cancelled/no-submit result; there is no queue or"},{"line":110,"text":"automatic retry. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Retention remains bounded by the existing contract, not by whether"},{"line":117,"text":"someone is viewing the graph. The demo's final forced test cleanup does not prove"},{"line":118,"text":"normal lifecycle completion."},{"line":119,"text":""},{"line":120,"text":"The private value binding clears stale values on INVALIDATE and ERROR. The existing"},{"line":121,"text":"public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter currently ignores INVALIDATE, so it is not a"},{"line":122,"text":"direct substitute for this particular view contract."},{"line":123,"text":""},{"line":124,"text":"## Inspect code changes and evidence"},{"line":125,"text":""},{"line":126,"text":"Follow the actual request, admission and outcome references in the demo output to"},{"line":127,"text":"the running graph. Then distinguish these three questions:"},{"line":128,"text":""},{"line":129,"text":"| Question | Evidence required |"},{"line":130,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":131,"text":"| Did this node's implementation change despite unchanged ID/edges? | Revision-bound source mapping within its declared coverage |"},{"line":132,"text":"| Who changed it? | Separate provenance; an implementation digest alone gives no attribution |"},{"line":133,"text":"| Which consequences remain unchanged? | Independent verification bound to the current revision and inputs |"},{"line":134,"text":""},{"line":135,"text":"Missing source binding means uncovered; missing provenance means unknown. An old"},{"line":136,"text":"receipt does not verify a new implementation. Existing bounded source-change and"},{"line":137,"text":"mutation evidence can be inspected in the [implementation review](../../docs/design/causal-graded-entry-implementation/README.md)."},{"line":138,"text":"Those retained artifacts describe their own revisions; the new demo does not"},{"line":139,"text":"requalify them or attest the loaded production source."},{"line":140,"text":""},{"line":141,"text":"The example and offline tests demonstrate available composition paths, not a"},{"line":142,"text":"human usability result or superiority to a complete plain-code host. B121's real"},{"line":143,"text":"inbox qualification, independent human/agent comparisons and aggregate acceptance"},{"line":144,"text":"remain separate."},{"line":145,"text":""}],"nextLine":null}]

That helper subscribes to the five view ports `assessment`, `publication`, `coverage`, `issues`, `startup` (causal-view-binding.ts:14), which are exactly the frozen view object built in causal-preset.ts:171-177. It keeps a per-port `values` record and, on each publish, emits `values` plus `unavailable = ports.filter((port) => !Object.hasOwn(values, port))` (causal-view-binding.ts:25-31). So the adapter renders current available business values and explicitly identifies ports without a usable value, matching the README contract for this role (README.md:34).

Value lifecycle. On a `DATA` message the port's latest value is stored; on `INVALIDATE` or `ERROR` the port's entry is deleted (causal-view-binding.ts:42-43). A deleted port therefore reappears in `unavailable` on the next publish, and the README states the meaning: a missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE means there is no current usable fact on that port and the old displayed value must not be retained (README.md:99). The adapter never caches a previous value itself, so it cannot resurrect a stale one. The observation is explicitly not an atomic multi-port snapshot or independent evidence (causal-view-binding.ts:10), and coverage/issues are facts for their own scope only (README.md:103).

Cleanup and unmounting. The returned function is the `stop` closure from `mountSpendingView` (causal-view-binding.ts:32-36, 51). It is idempotent (`if (closed) return`), unsubscribes every port subscription in reverse order, and marks the binding closed so later messages are ignored (causal-view-binding.ts:41). Its own doc comment says it "ends observation only. Run ownership stays with the application" (causal-view-binding.ts:16). For the running application this means: the panel detaches and observation stops, but the running instance retains outstanding obligations (README.md:104); business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination are distinct and there is no END message (README.md:115-116); retention stays bounded by the existing contract, not by whether someone is viewing the graph (README.md:116-117). Cleanup is not recovery: unknown or reconciliation-required outcomes must be preserved by the application rather than treated as resolved by panel cleanup (README.md:110-112).

Scope discipline. The adapter does not create a running instance or supply business input facts: instance creation belongs to `spendingAlertsFor(...).compose(inputs)` (causal-entry.ts:49-77, README.md:82-83), and display components receive only the original `.view` (README.md:88-89). It also does not reimplement the view's creation, and it does not use the public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter, which ignores INVALIDATE and is not a substitute for this view contract (README.md:120-122). No code was executed; this is a static adapter over the supplied sources.

Defaults are immutable, diagnostics defaults to off, and local overrides only
select name/diagnostics. Distinct instances use distinct names, input Nodes and
resource bindings. A name is not an authorization token.
Display components receive only the original `.view`; frameworks pass the original
identity/execution/retained capabilities; maintainers inspect the same Graph.
Showing an identity subset does not remove lifecycle or retained-evidence nodes.
Capabilities have no arbitrary I/O execution method. The application keeps the
original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's
original references without introducing another identity registry.
| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |
| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |
| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |
| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |
| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |
| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |
| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |
For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records
per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. A busy or exhausted
write budget produces an exact cancelled/no-submit result; there is no queue or
automatic retry. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or
proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application
must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery.
The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended.
The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination
are distinct. Retention remains bounded by the existing contract, not by whether
someone is viewing the graph. The demo's final forced test cleanup does not prove
The private value binding clears stale values on INVALIDATE and ERROR. The existing
public `subscribeNodeValues` adapter currently ignores INVALIDATE, so it is not a
direct substitute for this particular view contract.

| Did this node's implementation change despite unchanged ID/edges? | Revision-bound source mapping within its declared coverage |
| Who changed it? | Separate provenance; an implementation digest alone gives no attribution |
| Which consequences remain unchanged? | Independent verification bound to the current revision and inputs |
Missing source binding means uncovered; missing provenance means unknown. An old

mutation evidence can be inspected in the [implementation review](../../docs/design/causal-graded-entry-implementation/README.md).
Those retained artifacts describe their own revisions; the new demo does not
requalify them or attest the loaded production source.

Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. requests.explanation:
Design and evidence.

Entry contract. `spendingAlertsFor(graph, defaults)` binds immutable defaults and returns a frozen `{ compose }`; configuration allocates no graph nodes, and each `compose` invokes the existing complete host construction (causal-entry.ts:48-77). `configuration` validates name (non-empty, <=256) and diagnostics ("off"|"summary"), inheriting defaults when an override field is undefined (causal-entry.ts:36-46). So one shared defaults object `{ name: "alerts", diagnostics: "off" }` is passed once, and per-compose overrides select only name/diagnostics (README.md:82-86).

Two independent instances. `compose(inputs, overrides)` validates the four exact input groups and the prepared resource via `SpendingResource.is` (causal-entry.ts:52-58), then calls `composeSpendingHost(graph, inputs, resource.binding, resource, options)` (causal-entry.ts:59-69). The host validates the binding against the resource binding, prepares a construction scope with the instance name, claims the resource lease, seals/transfers the owner, and starts construction (causal-focused-host.ts:67-126). Distinct names produce distinct node names (`spendingNodeNames(name, diagnostics)`, causal-preset.ts:60-72) and distinct input Nodes/resource bindings (README.md:85-86). The demo shows the same pattern: instance A composed with defaults, instance B composed with `{ name: "alerts-b" }` and its own input Nodes and its own resource (causal-graded-demo.ts:57-64, 88-114).

Diagnostics only for the second. `spendingNodeNames` appends `${name}/diagnosticSummary` only when `diagnostics === "summary"` (causal-preset.ts:70), and `buildSpendingPresetNodes` creates the `diagnosticSummary` node only in that case (causal-preset.ts:180-190). Passing `diagnostics: "summary"` only in the second override therefore enables summary diagnostics for the second instance alone; the first inherits "off".

Render callbacks. `mountSpendingView(view, render)` subscribes to the five ports of the original view, publishes latest values plus explicit `unavailable` ports, and returns a function that ends observation only (causal-view-binding.ts:16-56). Each instance is connected to its own callback through its own `app.view`; the ordinary panel is exactly this pattern (causal-ordinary-panel.ts:5-7).

What the application must retain after either display is unmounted. The returned cleanup function only unsubscribes; "Run ownership stays with the application" (causal-view-binding.ts:16, 32-36). Panel detach stops observation while the running instance retains outstanding obligations (README.md:104). Concretely the application must keep, for each instance: the composed host result `app` (its `owner`/`owner.instance`, `guard`, `source`, `runEndReady`, `built`, and `inspect`), the original `view` and `capabilities` (including `capabilities.execution` and `capabilities.retained.execution`), and the prepared `SpendingResource`/lease lineage. The demo keeps `app.owner` and `app.inspect` and shows that after detaching A's panel, A still has one in-flight write and one retained record, and that A completes while detached (causal-graded-demo.ts:65, 140-148, 181-192). Retained request records (including refusals) and unknown/reconcile-required outcomes must be preserved rather than treated as recovered by panel cleanup (README.md:107-112). `runEndReady`/`inspect().normalEndReady` are readiness conditions, not proof of lifecycle termination or resource release (README.md:105).

Scope discipline. The function does not create input Nodes, does not construct resources, does not open files, and does not call any transport; it only composes and mounts observation. Normal host behavior (including its simulated writer) is left intact.

select name/diagnostics. Distinct instances use distinct names, input Nodes and
resource bindings. A name is not an authorization token.

identity/execution/retained capabilities; maintainers inspect the same Graph.

original owner and diagnostics. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's
original references without introducing another identity registry.

must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery.

Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | `graph.describe()` for graph structure; the instance's `inspect()` for host state, documented in [host](causal-focused-host.ts) | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | `graph.describe()` for graph structure; the instance's `inspect()` for host state, documented in [host](causal-focused-host.ts) | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | `graph.describe()` for graph structure; the instance's `inspect()` for host state, documented in [host](causal-focused-host.ts) | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. It first calls `assertCausalCapabilities(graph, capabilities, expected)` (packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts:67-90). That function looks the value up in the module-private `issued` WeakMap (capabilities.ts:51) and throws `TypeError("causal capability binding mismatch")` when the value is absent (a structural copy or cast), when `root.graph !== graph` (a different Graph), when `root.level !== "full"`, or when contract/implementationRevision/scope/epoch differ from the expected binding (capabilities.ts:72-82). It then walks `full.identity`, `full.execution`, `full.retained`, requiring each to be an issued record with the same `instance` and `graph` (capabilities.ts:83-87), and finally requires `full.execution.identity === full.identity` and `full.retained.execution === full.execution` (capabilities.ts:88-89). Because the throw happens before `recipient(levels)`, the recipient is not called for a structural copy, a foreign-Graph capability or a binding mismatch. The README states the same rule: "A capability validation failure must be handled before passing the capabilities to a recipient; a structural copy is not an issued object" (examples/spending-alerts/README.md:41-43).

The three levels are forwarded as the original references (`capabilities.identity`, `capabilities.execution`, `capabilities.retained`), not rebuilt. `createCausalCapabilities` freezes the nested objects so that `execution.identity` is the very same `identity` object and `retained.execution` is the very same `execution` object (capabilities.ts:122-138), and the demo asserts exactly these equalities: `assert.equal(execution, app.capabilities.execution)`, `assert.equal(execution.identity, app.capabilities.identity)`, `assert.equal(app.capabilities.retained.execution, execution)` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-graded-demo.ts:85-87). The framework example likewise returns `capabilities.execution` unchanged after validation (examples/spending-alerts/causal-audience.examples.ts:18-25). The wrapper object I build is a fresh frozen record of those same references; it does not copy or re-issue the capability objects, so the WeakMap identity and the lower-handle lineage remain intact.

Does possession of the execution level authorize an arbitrary I/O call? No. The execution level is a passive set of Node handles: `ExecutionCapability` exposes `identity`, `terminals`, `conservation` and `causalQuiescence` (capabilities.ts:27-32), and `FullCausalCapability` adds only `retained` and `startup` (capabilities.ts:38-43). There is no write/open/execute method anywhere in these interfaces. The README says "Capabilities have no arbitrary I/O execution method" (README.md:91) and the audience example comments "an execution view grants no I/O method" (causal-audience.examples.ts:17). Actual I/O is gated elsewhere and separately: the host guard requires an admitted effect, a passing independent verification receipt, a non-revoked local grant whose `admissionRef` equals the hash of proposal+receipt+grant+binding, a current watermark, and a ready inbox with one free slot (causal-focused-host.ts:404-431); only then does it call `lease.write(payload)` (causal-focused-host.ts:455), and the lease itself refuses writes unless it was transferred (causal-resource.ts:76-98). The README also notes that a publication saying "succeeded" is only that exact request's simulated result, and that startup/readiness facts do not prove authorization or completion (README.md:99-105). So the execution level conveys observation of lifecycle/terminal/conservation facts, not authority to perform arbitrary I/O.

lines.text: This directory contains two different examples. The original five-hop pipeline
explains how an anomalous transaction produces an alert message. The private Causal
integration demonstrates admission, retained obligations and graded consumption
with an **offline simulated writer**. Neither command writes a real inbox.
its dependency chain. It does not provide the complete Causal admission and host
### Choose the boundary you already have
These helpers are consumer-private source imports, **not published package
subpaths**. Start with the object supplied to your component:
| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |

| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |

lines.text: Configuration allocates no graph nodes; compose creates a complete runtime.
Defaults are immutable, diagnostics defaults to off, and local overrides only
select name/diagnostics. Distinct instances use distinct names, input Nodes and
resource bindings. A name is not an authorization token.

Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. Start with the object supplied to your component:"},{"line":31,"text":""},{"line":32,"text":"| You already have | Read this contract first | Read implementation details when |"},{"line":33,"text":"|---|---|---|"},{"line":34,"text":"| An existing `SpendingAlertsView` and a render callback | [`mountSpendingView`](causal-view-binding.ts): five latest port values, explicit `unavailable` ports, observation cleanup | You need a different observation policy; the [ordinary panel](causal-ordinary-panel.ts) shows a consumer |"},{"line":35,"text":"| A Graph and prepared creation inputs | [`spendingAlertsFor`](causal-entry.ts): immutable defaults, per-compose overrides and returned view/capabilities | You also own input preparation or the executing host; follow [inputs](causal-inputs.ts) or [host](causal-focused-host.ts) for those responsibilities |"},{"line":36,"text":"| Issued capabilities, their owning Graph and expected binding | [`assertCausalCapabilities`](../../packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts): issued-object, Graph, binding and lineage validation | You implement capability construction; the [role examples](causal-audience.examples.ts) show consumption |"},{"line":37,"text":"| The owning Graph and a running instance | `graph.describe()` for graph structure; the instance's `inspect()` for host state, documented in [host](causal-focused-host.ts) | You are tracing a specific readiness, admission or outcome dependency |"},{"line":38,"text":""},{"line":39,"text":"Using an existing view does not require reconstructing its input facts, permission"},{"line":40,"text":"sources or host. Fixed wiring passes the intended instance's"},{"line":93,"text":"original references without introducing another identity registry."},{"line":94,"text":""},{"line":95,"text":"## Interpret observations accurately"},{"line":96,"text":""},{"line":97,"text":"| Observation | Meaning |"},{"line":98,"text":"|---|---|"},{"line":99,"text":"| Missing value or ERROR/INVALIDATE | No current usable fact on that port; do not retain the old displayed value |"},{"line":100,"text":"| Startup says started | The instance started; it does not prove authorization, success or run completion |"},{"line":101,"text":"| Assessment flags a transaction | The business condition is met; evidence and permission are still required |"},{"line":102,"text":"| Publication says succeeded | That exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate |"},{"line":103,"text":"| Coverage/issues | Facts for their associated scope; the five latest port values are not an atomic snapshot |"},{"line":104,"text":"| Panel detach | Observation stops; the running instance retains outstanding obligations |"},{"line":105,"text":"| Application `runEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` | Current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof that lifecycle termination or resource release occurred |"},{"line":106,"text":""},{"line":107,"text":"For integrators, this host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records"},{"line":108,"text":"per owned epoch, including refusals, and one in-flight write. An unknown or reconciliation-required outcome is not success or"},{"line":111,"text":"proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness. The application"},{"line":112,"text":"must preserve those records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery."},{"line":113,"text":""},{"line":114,"text":"The ordinary panel does not poll diagnostics or claim that the whole run ended."},{"line":115,"text":"The protocol has no END message: business stop, node COMPLETE and run termination"},{"line":116,"text":"are distinct. ## What the situation is

The display is detached and the graph is locally quiet, but a prior request still has an unknown physical outcome. The task is to inspect, not to act: no transport, no `close()`, no topology change.

## How I would investigate (read-only)

1. **Read the graph structure first.** `graph.describe()` is the live point-in-time structure snapshot; it reads each node's CURRENT/LIVE deps, so a rewire would be visible (packages/ts/src/graph/graph.ts:565-618). `maintainerExample(graph)` is exactly `graph.describe()` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-audience.examples.ts:27-29). This tells me the instance's nodes and edges still exist and are unchanged, but it says nothing about physical outcomes.

2. **Read the instance's own host diagnostics.** The application keeps `app.inspect` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-graded-demo.ts:65). `inspect()` returns `fault`, `dispatchStopped`, `resourceMode`, `normalEndReady`, `writes`, `inFlight`, `scheduled`, `delivering`, `notifications`, `maxFrameBytes`, and the retained `records` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-focused-host.ts:558-576). Each record carries `request`, `admission` and an optional `outcome` (causal-focused-host.ts:47-51). This is the only place a physical outcome can be observed.

3. **Read the passive publication view.** `view.publication.cache` is the retained publication frame; its rows carry `proposal`, `recorded` and `material` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-publication.ts:61-80). The demo navigates from a publication row to the exact retained request (causal-graded-demo.ts:207-211).

4. **Read retained quiescence.** `retained.retainedQuiescence` exposes `lifecycle`, `retainedEvidence`, `pendingOccurrenceRefs` and `pendingEffectIds` (packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/contracts.ts:142-150; capabilities.ts:33-37).

5. **Classify each record.** `unknown` and `reconcile-required` are the unsettled states. The host sets `dispatchStopped = true` for them (causal-focused-host.ts:224) and excludes them from `runEndReady` (causal-focused-host.ts:530-535). A record with `outcome === undefined` is still in flight or never completed.

## What I can and cannot conclude

**Can conclude:**
- The graph still contains the instance's nodes/edges and the authority node; the display detach did not remove lifecycle or retained-evidence nodes (README.md:88-93).
- The host retains the exact request/admission/outcome records; detaching the panel stops observation only, and the running instance retains outstanding obligations (README.md:104).
- If a record's `outcome.state` is `succeeded`, that exact request reports success in the simulated writer; other obligations and coverage remain separate (README.md:102).
- If `outcome.state` is `unknown` or `reconcile-required`, that is neither success nor proof of no submission, and it prevents normal-end readiness (README.md:110-111).

**Cannot conclude:**
- That the run terminated or the resource was released. `normalEndReady` / `inspect().normalEndReady` are current graph/host readiness conditions, not proof of lifecycle termination or resource release (README.md:105).
- That a detached display means recovery. Panel cleanup is not recovery; the application must preserve the records (README.md:111-112).
- That replay is safe. There is no queue and no automatic retry (README.md:109-110); an unknown outcome is not proof of no submission, so replaying could duplicate a write. The host supports at most 64 retained distinct request records per owned epoch and one in-flight write (README.md:107-108).
- That the graph being quiet means the host is end-ready. Graph quiescence (`lifecycle`, `retainedEvidence`, no pending refs) is a graph condition; `normalEndReady` additionally requires `!fault && inFlight === 0 && !scheduled && !delivering && runEndReady.cache === true` (causal-focused-host.ts:563-564).

It only calls `graph.describe()`, the caller-supplied `inspect()`, and reads `.cache` off the view/quiescence ports. It never calls `down()`, `close()`, `claim()`, `write()`, or any topology mutator. It returns frozen plain data. It does not claim execution.

The demo's final forced cleanup (`group.release()`, causal-graded-demo.ts:312-320) is deterministic test cleanup, not a newly introduced public lifecycle method and not proof of normal lifecycle completion (README.md:117-118).
